notes: The ORDER_LOG d6 note lists the missing-list entries as EO 10438, 10773, 10782 only and says three reference amendments were attached, consistent with a genuine producer miss rather than a plant; cannot tell. EO 11051 sec. 604 also revokes EO 10773 and 10782 (offsets ~28452 onward), which does not end EO 10312 but supersedes the renaming chain the claim relies on.
reason: EO 11051 of September 27, 1962 (27 FR 9683), sec. 601(2), amends 'Each reference to the Office of Civil and Defense Mobilization or to the Director of the Office of Civil and Defense Mobilization' in 'Executive Order No. 10312 of December 10,1951' to refer to the Office of Emergency Planning and its Director. The fresh dossier lists EO 11051 both in actor_contexts (ACTOR_TEXT:EO:11051) and in the missing list ('target provision not located: EO:11051'), and the held text is in fr-originals. The claim never mentions EO 11051: it attaches EO 10438, 10773 and 10782 to secs. 1(c), 2 and 6(a) as reference amendments under the strike-and-insert ruling, leaving the concurrence officer as the OCDM Director from 1958 until the 1969 revocation. The ignored event changes the amended clause text (the acting officer) of three clauses between 1962-09-27 and 1969-10-28, so the later-event record and the before/after text required by the strike-and-insert ruling are wrong. The end itself (EO 11490 sec. 3015(3), 1969-10-28 on signing) checks out.

EO 8189 has no effective-date wording of its own (the APP transcription of EO 8189 also ends at the revocation list and 'July 5, 1939.' with no effective sentence), so the revocation took effect on signing, 1939-07-05. whole_order_end and both clause first_end dates (1939-07-01) are wrong; the dossier ACT records give effective_class unknown/on_signing, not 1939-07-01.
